blocks.text: Recursive Feature Elimination closed out the wrapper method family by directly using a model own internal ranking, but still genuinely wrapped that ranking inside an external, iterative removal loop, retraining across many rounds. Embedded methods open this module third and final family, going one real step further, building feature selection directly into a single model training run, with no separate search loop wrapped around it at all.

This topic covers exactly how embedded methods genuinely produce feature selection as a direct byproduct of training, where this family genuinely sits in the real cost spectrum first previewed back in Filter Methods, the key, genuine difference between this family and the RFE technique covered just before it, and a preview of the three specific embedded techniques, Lasso, tree based selection, and feature importance, that close out this entire module.
1. How Embedded Methods Actually Work

blocks.alt: The model is trained once, with selection happening built in

blocks.text: An embedded method genuinely trains one model, exactly once, and feature selection genuinely emerges as a direct byproduct of that single training process, rather than requiring any separate scoring pass beforehand, exactly what filter methods do, or any repeated retraining loop afterward, exactly what wrapper methods do. The model itself, during its own genuine training, decides which features actually matter.

This is genuinely the defining, core idea of this entire family, selection is not a separate step bolted onto training at all, it is genuinely woven directly into the training process itself, happening automatically as a natural consequence of how the specific algorithm actually learns.
2. Where This Family Sits in the Real Cost Spectrum

blocks.alt: Filter is fastest, embedded sits in between, wrapper is slowest

blocks.text: Filter methods genuinely require zero model training at all, the fastest option, but genuinely blind to how any actual model would use the features. Wrapper methods genuinely train many models, the slowest, most expensive option, but genuinely reflect real, actual model performance directly. Embedded methods genuinely sit precisely in between, training exactly one model, no more, no fewer.

This genuine middle position is exactly why embedded methods are often the genuinely most practical, appealing choice in a real project, capturing much of wrapper methods real, model aware accuracy, without paying anywhere close to their real, often severe computational cost.

blocks.text: 3. The Key, Genuine Difference From RFE

blocks.alt: RFE retrains repeatedly while embedded methods need only one training pass

blocks.text: Recursive Feature Elimination, covered in the previous topic, genuinely already used a model own coefficients or importance scores to guide selection, which might sound similar to embedded methods at first. The genuine, real difference lies in the loop, RFE genuinely wraps that model ranking inside an external, iterative removal process, retraining the model again and again across many separate rounds.

Embedded methods genuinely skip that entire external loop, training the model exactly once, and reading off which features mattered directly from that single, completed training run, with no repeated retraining involved at all.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: RFE and embedded methods both genuinely use a model own internal ranking, the real difference is the loop. RFE retrains repeatedly around that ranking; embedded methods read it once, directly from a single training run.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example

A genuine embedded method in its simplest form, reading feature importance directly off a single trained model, with no loop or repeated retraining involved at all, shows this family core idea concretely.

code.content:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
model.fit(X, y)

print("Feature importances:", dict(zip(X.columns, model.feature_importances_)))

blocks.text: A single call to fit genuinely trains this random forest exactly once, and feature_importances_ is genuinely already available immediately afterward, no separate scoring pass, no repeated retraining loop, square_feet and bedrooms genuinely receiving far higher importance than the deliberately irrelevant shoe size column.

blocks.text: 5. Three Genuine Embedded Techniques Ahead

blocks.alt: Embedded methods include lasso, tree-based selection, and feature importance

blocks.text: Lasso, covered next, genuinely uses a specific kind of regularization that drives some feature coefficients to exactly zero during training, effectively excluding them automatically, no manual threshold or ranking needed. Tree based selection covers how decision trees and ensembles naturally compute a genuine importance score for every feature as a direct, automatic consequence of how they build their splits.

Feature Importance, closing out this entire module, ties these ideas together into a genuine, general framework, covering how importance gets extracted differently across model types, and introducing permutation importance, a genuinely model agnostic alternative that works even when a model provides no built in importance score at all.
6. Genuinely Model Aware, Like Wrapper Methods

blocks.alt: Embedded methods are genuinely model aware

blocks.text: Because selection genuinely happens as part of actual model training, embedded methods share wrapper methods real, genuine advantage, the resulting feature set genuinely reflects how the actual, specific model in use really relies on each feature, not a generic, model agnostic statistical score computed independently of any real model behavior.

This genuine model awareness is exactly what filter methods, covered at the start of this module, structurally cannot offer, embedded methods genuinely close that specific gap, without paying wrapper methods real, full computational price to get there.
7. Genuinely Fast, Like Filter Methods

Because only one single model training pass is genuinely required, with no repeated retraining across candidate subsets or rounds, embedded methods genuinely share filter methods real speed advantage as well, at least relative to the many models wrapper methods genuinely require.

This combination, genuine model awareness paired with genuine, real efficiency, is exactly why embedded methods are often the genuinely best practical default in a real project, when the chosen model genuinely supports one of the specific techniques covered in the remainder of this module.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: When the model already planned for deployment supports Lasso or a tree based approach, genuinely reach for an embedded method first, before considering the added real cost of a full wrapper method search.
